markers.reading: The party crosses Jita Square near sunset; at archive entry the DM specifies sunset is still about half an hour away.

evidence.quote: Okay. So as the sun sets you find yourself walking across Jita Square, the largest and most central plaza in Tokra.
I mean, sunset’s in like half an hour. The sun is setting in the sky as you enter the archives.

markers.reading: A few minutes pass in the archives while the party waits for Ardan.

evidence.quote: A few minutes later while you’re waiting, Ardan comes down the stairs and he’s, "You're back."—

duration.basis: Narrated wait before Ardan comes downstairs

markers.reading: The archive conversation has taken 15–20 minutes; sunset has now occurred and the moon is rising.

evidence.quote: So you. You've been talking for 15, 20 minutes now, and now it's set. The moon beginning to inch over the horizon. So where do you want to all go?
See okay. So Kenzo and Seeker head out the front door into Jita Square, the open plaza now. You’re just beginning to see the faint glimmer of moonlight as the moon rises above the walls of the city.

markers.reading: By the time the dwarves help carry Dag to the well, Seeker’s one-minute Quicksand has ended.

evidence.quote: No, that spell only lasts for a minute, so it’s turned back into regular stone now.

duration.basis: Narration establishes that the full one-minute spell expired

markers.note: This measures spell time spanning the end of combat and its aftermath, not an additional minute after the family conversation.

Unknown: Yeah.
So Fallthra returns with a a whole chicken. Plucked and carved, like this is like the cold chicken they, they roasted, right, yesterday or something, and were saving for a nice meal, yeah.

Until maybe five minutes, as, as now the water begins to freeze more and more, Fallthra, unable to hold herself back, just rushes forward and starts crying.

markers.reading: After hearing distant howls, Wellby listens from the roof for another 10–15 minutes before the last howl and silence.

evidence.quote: While this has been happening down below, Wellby, you've been you know scouting from the roof.

This is like like the edge of your hearing. This is probably a mile or two away. Not necessarily getting closer. And there's 1000 strong army camped between the noise and the town. And you listen for another 10, 15 minutes and there's one more long echoing howl that again maybe could be a coyote but there's a chill to it that strikes you as something different.

And then the noise goes silent.

DM: Coming almost directly northwest of where you are and probably a good mile off.

duration.basis: DM narrates additional listening after the initial distant howls

markers.reading: A few more minutes of conversation pass while Wellby checks the receding howls.

evidence.quote:
Speaking of giving away position, as it's been a few minutes of conversation, are those howls coming closer or further or gone?

Unknown: Gone.

DM: If anything, they were getting further away.

duration.basis: Wellby explicitly advances the ongoing conversation and the DM resolves the current howls

markers.reading: Kenzo completes his return to the Lakan monastery just before midnight.

evidence.quote: Ah yes. Yes, it's actually a pretty quiet night, especially once you get south of the city. You arrive back to the monastery maybe and just before midnight. The monastery is still and calm.

time.basis: DM’s stated arrival relative to the approaching midnight

markers.reading: All four sleep in their respective lodgings, gain a long rest, and wake on the morning of July 2.

evidence.quote:
This is gonna be the transition to morning so yeah.

Delwath: Just moving ahead so—

DM: So, as you all drift off to sleep in your respective places um ah, you get a long rest.
And you wake up the morning of July 2 now, um, Seeker, Wellby and Delwath in Kirian's, in your rooms at Kirian's, Kenzo in the monastery.

time.basis: July 2 and morning are spoken; year 1748 is inherited from the session YAML

markers.note: The proposed 4–5 a.m. return at u1839–u1843 is not separately confirmed. The completed transition supplies morning and rest benefits without establishing every actor’s bedtime.

And she hands you a map. I didn't manage to put this on Roll20, but it is it is here.

markers.reading: The veterans and party share a minute’s quiet over tea after the stories about Govir.

evidence.quote: Drink tea. Kind of quiet pervades the Group for a minute.

markers.reading: During Seeker’s remote viewing, it is still relatively early morning and Illyan finishes a meal.

evidence.quote: Okay, so this is, yeah, the tent of a Dunmari commander. There's like papers spread around. There's, um, it's still relatively early in the morning, and he seems to be just finishing up a meal.

markers.note: This dates the observed current scene; it does not move Seeker from the inn.

markers.reading: During Clairvoyance a minute or two passes without activity; Illyan then leaves after his ring glows and returns a minute later with Drusa.

evidence.quote: Nothing seems to be happening for a minute or two—
10 minutes and then he like looks down at his hand, and you can see that he has a ring that’s glowing, and he curses some expletive and he gets up and runs out of the tent.
A minute later um he comes back with a Chardonian woman a young ish woman who like is looking around and then points up directly—

markers.reading: The party leaves Tokra riding north just after lunch; the proposed ride to the fort is diverted before arrival.

evidence.quote: So you leave Tokra, riding north just after lunch.

It's maybe only a two-hour ride to the fort, and, um, and as you, as you sort of head in that direction, um you pass quickly through like the sort of farmland at the outskirts of Tokra and come to an area that seems like there's no people around. There's no herds in the distance. There's not even any animals. It just seems quiet.

Yeah although it'd be interesting to see where the other end of this trail goes to.

Delwath: Yeah I think we should go south.

Seeker: So it's going to intersect the road—

Wellby: And if it continues does it like go to some access point to the city or? Yeah. Or, yeah, I'm convinced. Without me— We know what’s out the north end.

Seeker: If—

DM: You follow the trail South for maybe a mile, two miles, two and a half miles, you can see the walls of the city now. You’re a bit to the west of the city, and there’s—still a bit west of the city and a bit north of the of the road, maybe maybe half mile from the city when the trail turns abruptly east. Continues for about 200 yards and then stops in—there's like a little—the terrain here, like, it's mostly plains. You're sort of to the, to the west of the city. There's not so much farms. markers.note: The two-hour ride is an estimate to the fort, which the party does not reach; it is not counted as completed travel.

markers.reading: Seeker’s excavation opens a hole through the tunnel roof in about two minutes.

evidence.quote:
Okay, you walk about 1,500 feet through this dirt passageway. At times you need to like get down and crawl, like there’s been parts that have been shored up.

DM: But this is a you know, this is a crude excavation. It goes pretty deep like slopes down pretty steeply from here, and then it's just passing through the sort of the Earth.

yamlCheck.dateAnchor: July 2 is independently spoken at waking. The opening July 1 date and year 1748 are conditional on YAML; the earlier morning recap does not independently extend the played span.
yamlCheck.explanation: The near-sunset opening, completed overnight transition to July 2 morning and ensuing post-lunch exploration support one date boundary, matching July 1–2. Historical attacks, veteran memories, dreams not played out, and travel forecasts do not add days.
